headline: Chip Rout Leaves Wall Street Bruised as Geopolitics Crowd the Week Ahead
body_html:
Wall Street ended Friday's session, November 20, in retreat. Of the 663 stocks we track, 554 fell and only 103 rose. Semiconductors were the epicenter, dropping 10.02% as the artificial-intelligence selloff intensified. One report said the rout has erased the Nasdaq's gains for 2026, with Alphabet a rare bright spot in big tech.

The damage spread well beyond chips. Financials lost 3.53%, energy 3.3%, industrials 3.17% and materials 3.16%, while software slid 2.1%, healthcare 1.63% and consumer names 1.37%. Homebuilders were the lone sector in positive territory, up 0.32%. Gap climbed 11.44% and Buckle gained 5.67%, pockets of strength in apparel. Applied Optoelectronics, Sandisk, Celestica, Alpha and Omega, Bloom Energy and Credo each fell more than 15%.

Monday, November 23, brings the first chance to judge whether sellers are exhausted or still in control. Traders will also track the Middle East, where Iran talk of diplomacy collides with Washington's hard line and Houthi missile fire targets Saudi Arabia, and the Ukraine diplomacy involving Moscow.

briefs.headline: Optical and memory names lead the plunge
briefs.body: Applied Optoelectronics fell 16.55% and Sandisk 16.05%, with Credo Technology and Alpha and Omega Semiconductor also down more than 15%. The moves show how violently the selloff hit companies tied to AI infrastructure. Monday's open will test whether buyers step in.

briefs.headline: Apparel retailers swim against the tide
briefs.body: Gap jumped 11.44% and Buckle rose 5.67%, the standout winners in a market where most stocks fell. Spectrum Brands also gained 6.3%. Consumer shares overall slipped 1.37%, so the strength looked stock-specific rather than sector-wide.

briefs.headline: Iran signals openness to talks; Washington balks
briefs.body: Iran's foreign minister said Tehran wants diplomacy to end the war, but President Trump called the terms unacceptable. The Treasury meanwhile sanctioned Iranian intermediaries said to collect oil revenue. Any shift in tone could move energy shares, which fell 3.3% Friday.

briefs.headline: Houthi fire unsettles Saudi Arabia
briefs.body: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh, and Saudi-led forces struck a Yemeni port. The Houthis have also warned airlines away from the kingdom. The attacks add to worries about a proposed US-Saudi nuclear power pact.

briefs.headline: Trump upbeat on Putin, cautious on guarantees
briefs.body: President Trump described good talks with Russia's Putin over Ukraine but held back from offering security guarantees. Investors will look for signs that a settlement is nearer, or that the gap between the sides remains wide, in the days ahead.

briefs.headline: Job-market 'coiled spring' may snap open
briefs.body: One labor expert argues that pent-up resignations could lift turnover as workers who have held back start moving. A rise in quits would signal more confidence among employees. It would also add a new wrinkle to how traders read the economy.
